ideas.text: An AI that detects a reorg coming 6 weeks before the announcement based on unusual 1:1 scheduling patterns.
A bot that translates 'exciting structural changes' into a probability distribution of what might actually be happening.
An app that maps the new org chart and identifies who gained power, who lost it, and who got a new title with the same salary.
A tool that detects when your job description changed but your compensation didn't and files the paperwork.
An AI that figures out which of your current recurring meetings no longer make sense post-reorg and cancels them.
A bot that detects 'we're streamlining for focus' and translates it by department affected.
An app that runs a personal impact analysis every time a reorg is announced and tells you what to do in the next 48 hours.
A tool that detects when you're on a team that has been reorganized 4 times in 3 years and suggests therapy.
An AI that identifies which of your relationships, projects, and institutional knowledge just became irrelevant overnight.
A bot that detects when a reorg creates a new layer of management between you and the people who matter.
An app that predicts your new manager's leadership style from their LinkedIn, Glassdoor reviews, and public speaking clips.
A tool that converts 'right-sizing' into a headcount number before the company does.
An AI that detects when 'this is about our strategy, not performance' is specifically about performance.
A bot that finds all the tasks that used to belong to someone who was laid off and assigns them to the correct new owner.
An app that detects which post-reorg org chart was actually finalized versus which one was released while still being negotiated.
A tool that identifies the three people in the new structure whose approval now matters more than before.
An AI that detects reorg survivor guilt and recommends taking the rest of Thursday off.
A bot that generates your first email to a new manager with the right balance of enthusiasm and professional reserve.
An app that monitors the announcement FAQ page for edits that add information leadership forgot to include.
A tool that detects when a reorg was announced at 4pm on a Friday and calculates the intentionality of that timing.
An AI that identifies which recurring commitments your previous manager made that your new manager doesn't know about.
A bot that generates a 60-day game plan for establishing yourself in the new structure before anyone forms a wrong impression.
An app that estimates how long it takes your company's reorgs to stabilize based on historical pattern data.
A tool that detects when the announced reason for a reorg doesn't match the observable outcome and files it.
An AI that maps who you need to re-introduce yourself to and in what order after a significant structural change.
A bot that detects when 'integration' is happening and estimates the cultural collision damage before it occurs.
An app that tracks which strategic priorities survived the reorg and which were quietly retired without a funeral.
A tool that detects when all-hands Q&As about reorgs are moderated to avoid the one question everyone has.
An AI that identifies the work that was being done by someone who just left that will become a crisis in 60 days.
A bot that converts the reorg announcement slide deck into a list of things it chose not to say.
An app that detects when two teams being merged have never actually spoken to each other.
A tool that monitors post-reorg Glassdoor submissions and sends an alert when the keywords start clustering.
An AI that estimates how many employees will quietly update their LinkedIn in the 72 hours after a reorg announcement.
A bot that detects when 'we're not replacing the role, we're evolving it' is corporate for 'we're replacing the role.'
An app that generates a list of reasonable questions to ask your new manager in the first 1:1 without seeming scared.
A tool that detects when a reorg created an accountability gap and fills it with a named owner before things break.
An AI that estimates your role's security based on how many times it was mentioned in the all-hands slides.
A bot that tracks which teams have been 'centralized' by the last 3 reorgs and asks how centralization is working.
An app that helps you explain the third reorg in 18 months to a candidate you're trying to recruit without lying.
A tool that detects when a reorg announcement uses 'empowerment' and cross-references it with who lost budget.
An AI that identifies which projects are now politically unsafe to be associated with under the new structure.
A bot that detects when a reorg is actually a demotion renamed as a lateral move and estimates by how much.
An app that generates the Slack message you need to send to 40 people saying 'heads up, I report to someone new.'
A tool that detects when a restructuring solved no problems but created three new reporting ambiguities.
An AI that predicts which reorg-era promises will be forgotten within 90 days and generates a reminder calendar.
A bot that detects when a company's fifth reorg announcement uses the same language as the first one.
An app that identifies which team just got 'elevated to report directly to the CEO' and what that actually means.
A tool that tracks the half-life of org charts at your company and sets your expectations accordingly.
An AI that compiles all the things promised during the reorg town hall and schedules monthly check-ins for each.
A bot that sends a personalized 'hope you're doing okay' to the 3 people most visibly affected by today's announcement.
An app that detects when a new team name was added without adding any clarity about what the team does.
A tool that identifies when two people now have the same title and no one decided who owns what yet.
An AI that converts 'we're becoming one unified team' into a Venn diagram of who will actually work together.
A bot that detects reorg fatigue in pulse survey data and suggests a 90-day moratorium on restructuring.
